literal: All things acquired making others weep will depart making the owner weep; even if lost, things of a good nature will yield benefits later.
translation: Everything acquired by causing others to weep will depart causing tears; but righteous gains, even if they are lost at first, will yield good fruits in the end.
modern: பிறர் அழும்படி துன்புறுத்திப் பெற்ற செல்வங்கள் எல்லாம் தாம் அழும்படியாக நம்மை விட்டுப் போய்விடும்; ஆனால், நல்ல வழியில் வந்தவை இழக்கப்பட்டாலும் பின்னர் நன்மையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts wealth acquired through unethical means with wealth acquired through righteous means. The poet states that wealth gained by causing distress and tears to others will eventually vanish, bringing tears to the one who gathered it. Conversely, wealth earned through righteous deeds might be lost initially, but it will eventually yield beneficial results in the future. The repetition of the word 'அழ' (weeping) emphasizes the poetic justice of karmic retribution, where the pain inflicted on others returns to the perpetrator.
